### D.9 Interior invariance

The interior invariance formula is defined as:

`for all ticks t:   H_actors( t | vel = v, world = w )  ==  H_actors( t | vel = 0, world = 0 )   for every admissible (v, w)`

Equivalently, the interior view is a function with no argument in the `bodies` table: `interior_view(actors, layout.state)`. This is the registered rule `interior_invariance`.

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `H_actors` | bytes | canonical bytes of the `actors` table (BDY-32 order) | the kernel's `state_hash` (kernel D.12), compared per table | the actor table's contribution to the hash |
| `v`, `w` | int pairs | D.7 ranges | the acceptance fixture | any admissible exterior velocity and pose |

**Output Range:** equality at every tick. The whole-block `state_hash` of `body.state` differs when `world_*` or `vel_*` differ, BY DESIGN (the `bodies` rows are part of the block); a criterion written against the whole-block hash would fail falsely, so the criterion compares the actor-table contribution (and `layout.state`).

**Example (acceptance fixture):** give the avatar's body `vel = (3, 0)`, run 600 ticks of a scripted command stream, and run the identical stream at `vel = (0, 0)`: the `actors` bytes match at every tick, while the `bodies` row differs by `world.x = 1,800` at tick 600. A lint asserts that nothing reachable from `solid_in`, the actor loop of `body.integrate`, the Emitter, Suit or the interior camera pose names `world_` or `vel_`.

**CR-15. Control plane** (host-local, not commands): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; CR-18)*, `request_shutdown`. Callers: Save/Load, the pause/Chart Table UI (host-local call), boot code. **Timing** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a request is recorded when made — from any phase, from a hook, from a P5 handler, or from outside a tick (a UI call between frames) — and served at the **next boundary**, where a boundary is the P6 of a tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service (run before any tick of the frame and, while `PAUSED`, every frame), whichever comes first; the call itself never changes state. `request_shutdown` is accepted from **every state except `SHUTTING_DOWN`** (including `BOOTING`, `LOADING` and `SAVING`; in those it is served at the boundary that follows the atomic step). Requests reaching the same boundary are applied in arrival order, never coalesced: a `request_pause` then a `request_resume` on one boundary leaves the kernel `RUNNING` with no paused service cycle run; a caller that needs a definite state re-issues the state it wants (Chart Table CT-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus (ASK-CT-9))*. **`request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash = none)`** (K-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1: `restore_epoch` is supplied by Save/Load, which has already incremented it and durably written the slot header; the kernel holds it read-only for the session, exposes it in the `kernel.clock` read view (CR-8) and rejects a value outside the u32 range in its pre-check, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`)*: when an expected hash is given, the kernel recomputes `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` (D.12) after the last `post_restore()`, inside `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, and reports `{T, computed_hash, match}` to the requester; Save/Load derives its EXACT / REBASED / mismatch verdict from it (SL-12). A mismatch is **not** a `FAULTED` transition — release plays on; policy is the requester's. Save/Load does not use restore-into-`PAUSED` for this window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (K-4))*. **Control-plane read access:** a control-plane caller is not one of the CR-10 subscriber classes; Save/Load (the one such caller at MVP) may read `kernel.clock`, the Controller's per-seat `loco_state`, the Graph's `read_view.failures()` and an optional Attention `SIM` read view, and receives end-of-tick notifications, all read in the tick boundary in which it issues a request; it never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT`, never submits commands and never holds a `WriteScope` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-13))*. In VS-B a guest's pause or save *request* is a command defined by Session or Save/Load, validated on the host, which then calls the control API.

**CR-16. Pause semantics.** `PAUSED` stops the tick but not rendering. While paused, submit accepts only types flagged `allowed_when_paused` by their owner, and **only non-diegetic actions may carry the flag** (save, settings, resume, menu navigation) — no gameplay verb that changes `SIM` state is allowed while paused, so a solo player cannot equip, repair or re-route with time stopped mid-tell (Dread Before Chaos), and solo pause behaves like co-op's overlay-only pause; a paused-allowed command may write only blocks registered `gameplay = false` **and** named in the type's `writes_blocks` (boot-checked, CR-6; the `WriteScope` issued in the paused cycle carries exactly that set, and a write outside it is refused and counted as `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`), never a `SIM` gameplay block *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; everything else is rejected `PAUSED` immediately, never queued, so there is no burst on resume. Admitted paused-allowed commands are dispatched by a **paused service cycle** that runs P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 with no P3 and with `T` unchanged, **once per rendered frame while `PAUSED`** (the paused boundary, which also serves control-plane requests), so a save or a menu action takes effect without advancing simulated time. At MVP no command type sets the flag; the cycle is a retained seam that only test fixtures exercise (CR-2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Commands already queued when the pause is honoured are neither dispatched by the service cycle nor rejected: they wait, in order, for the first `RUNNING` tick after resume. **Pause is single-player only**: in co-op a menu cannot stop a shared sim — VS-B treats pause as a UI overlay with the kernel `RUNNING`. The Chart Table GDD must not assume "pick a target" happens while paused. Relationship to the scene tree's pause → ADR.

**CR-17. Bounds and overload behaviour.** At most `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK` processed per tick, the rest waiting FIFO. `QUEUE_CAPACITY` total and `PER_ISSUER_CAPACITY` per issuer; beyond that `QUEUE_FULL` at admission — never silent drop, never unbounded growth. Catch-up runs at most `MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` ticks per frame, then lets simulated time lag rather than spiral (lag above `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` is dropped at the end of the frame, D.5); a lag counter is exposed to diagnostics. P3 exceeding `STEP_BUDGET_MS` logs the slowest hooks but the tick completes. A command older than its type's `max_age_ticks` is rejected `STALE`, so a hitch cannot unleash a second of stale intents. At the defaults `STALE` is unreachable from local ingress (the queue can hold a command at most 8 ticks and `T` does not advance while paused or saving); it is a VS-B seam for remote-stamped ticks, guarded locally by a "never stale" invariant test (Section E; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

**CR-18. Snapshot semantics.** A snapshot is taken only at a tick boundary (P6), covers all `persist` blocks at the same T, and records `(T, per-block schema_version)`. Capture is synchronous and in memory with the tick halted (`SAVING`), and **atomic within a single boundary service — `SAVING` never spans a frame**; file I/O is Save/Load's and off the critical path → ADR. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Restore replaces all `WORLD`-scoped persisted blocks atomically and leaves `PROFILE`-scoped blocks untouched (Pillar 5: losing the ship or a body never loses knowledge); partial restore within a scope is unsupported; failure aborts to `FAULTED` with pre-restore state intact where possible. With join-in-progress deferred, the same snapshot/restore contract is VS-B's guest transfer at session start, so it must be complete and cheap. **New game (K-2):** a new game passes through `LOADING`: every block takes `default_state()`, Save/Load's `new_game(world_seed)` sets `world_seed` into `kernel.clock` *(a new game is entered by the control-plane call `request_new_game(world_seed, restore_epoch = 0)`, valid from `RUNNING`, `PAUSED` and `FAULTED` as well as at first boot, so a second new game in one process — for example "death = restart from the last autosave" when no autosave exists yet — has a path; it flushes the queue with `Dropped(RELOAD)` exactly like `request_restore`, resets `T` to 0, installs the supplied epoch (a fresh slot's header starts at 0) and leaves `PROFILE`-scoped blocks untouched: Pillar 5, a new world never loses knowledge; what a new crew keeps is Open Question 13, Save/Load's) (Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, then each owner that registered an `init_world(world_seed)` step runs it in `restore_after` order under one `WriteScope`, before `post_restore()`; at MVP the world build is Web Map & Transit's `init_world` (WM-7), which calls the Layout, Graph and Body mutators in its fixed order *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-18) and web-map-and-transit)*.

**CR-19. Fault channel, violations and build profiles** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; replaces the earlier 'throws / asserts' model)*. GDScript has no `try`/`catch`: a runtime script error is printed by the engine, aborts the function it occurred in and hands control back to the caller with a default value the caller cannot distinguish from a result; and `assert()` is compiled out of release exports. The kernel therefore **never relies on an exception or an assertion for control flow**, and every behaviour in this document is identical in debug and release unless a clause calls it a `STRICT_DEBUG` extra.

**EM-7 — The beam changes only on committed state.** `toggle_beam` is owned by Emitter State and fixed by the Controller (PC-5, PC-2): `actor` = the seat's beam emitter id, `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120, origin `PLAYER`. The payload carries no state (it is a toggle: the `beam_toggle` press flips `switch_on`), so a rejected or duplicated command can never desynchronise the intent. Its apply flips `switch_on` in P2 of tick T; `emitter.place` in P3 of the same tick computes `output_pm`; the committed light therefore changes in the tick the toggle applies, with zero internal latency. The click and the hand's switch animation pre-play immediately (Presenter); **the light changes only on committed state and the Presenter never predicts beam state** (PC-5), because the beam is the human-channel anchor and may never lie, not even for one flicker. The seat's beam id is allocated at boot by E9; the session owner enters it in the kernel binding table (`PlayerId -> {controlled entity IDs}`) through the host-only API (CR-7: "a boot step in MVP"), which is what lets `toggle_beam` carry `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`. === L275
**LY-17 — Recording a cut; detach and body ids.** `detach_section(seam_id, boundary_mode)` (LM3, Class A) runs after the Graph's `cut_detach` (LSG:172). It marks the weld row `CUT_SEALED` or `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`; sets both sockets `CAPPED` (SEALED) or `CUT_OPEN` (RAGGED); then runs connected components over the ACTIVE `welds[]` in ascending `section_id`. The component containing the body's `origin_section_id` keeps its `body_id`; the other component receives a NEW `body_id` from `next_body_id` (KRN:197: "Detach allocates a new body ID from the Layout block") and its `origin_section_id` is **`m`, the minimum `section_id` of that component** (D.12 — the same section whose origin becomes the new frame origin); its offsets are re-based so its frame origin is its minimum-id section's origin (D.12). **Dirty keys and versions (the rule of LY-12 d):** `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<kept>`, `BODY/<new>`, and `SEC/<id>` plus a `version` and `static_version` bump for **every section whose socket state changed (both sections of the seam, the kept-side section even though it does not move) and every moved section**. If the hatch was open when it was cut (`area` > 0), the kept section's LEAF slot goes inactive and its PLATE goes active in the same apply, so the bump is what tells a version-keyed consumer that a light gap has become a solid plate. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Entombment: who owns the guarantee that no actor stands where the PLATE materialises** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the severity is RECOMMENDED because the crisis cut and lethal friendly fire make the state reachable and AC-28 treats such an overlap as a Body defect)*: **Layout performs no actor check** (it reads nothing from `body.state`, LY-18) and `apply` places the PLATE unconditionally. On the **CHANNEL cut path** the guarantee is Assembly's: the completion `validate` blocks the cut outright (`MSA.CUT_BLOCKED`, MSA-21) while any crewmate's foot box overlaps the open hatch passage, using `detach_preview`'s `rects[]` (the PLATE footprint) as the test region. On the **crisis cut path** (a cut that does not run through the channel) the guarantee is **Body's**: before the cut's `apply`, or in the same tick's `body.integrate`, Body ejects any foot box overlapping a SOLID PLATE footprint to the nearest legal row on the side of its own section, or the crisis cut is refused; which of the two Body does is Body's to rule (routed in Open Questions, OQ-LY-ENTOMB). Until it rules, the crisis path has no stated owner beyond this routing. `detach_section` also checks `CAPACITY` in its validate (LY-29). Returns `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}`. **A cut through a compartment is not representable:** a cut is requested only by `seam_id` (LSG:849 "Cuts happen only along seams, never through a compartment"), so Layout has no "cut here" geometry input. A cut never splits gas by a volume ratio because a compartment belongs to one section (LSG:172).

**BDY-24 — The hatch-cap hazard: refuse on player origin, never displace.** After a cut the socket's hatch is a SOLID `HULL` rectangle (`CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN`, LY-15), so an actor standing in the hatch passage ends inside a footprint — a real hazard no designed GDD names. (i) Body publishes the pure read `actors_overlapping(body_id, rects[]) -> actor_id[]` (ascending); Assembly's `validate` of a PLAYER-origin cut rejects while it is non-empty for the seam's two hatch rectangles (the reason code is Assembly's: `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED`, adopted in MSA-21). **Origin is read as Assembly's `cause`** (consistency pass 2026-10-27, routed from `modular-ship-assembly.md` C7): hooks submit SYSTEM-origin commands only (KRN CR-3), so every channel-completed cut reaches P2 as SYSTEM-origin; throughout this GDD "PLAYER-origin cut" means `seam_cut {cause CHANNEL}` (rejects, at begin, handoff and completion) and "SYSTEM-origin cut" means `seam_cut {cause CASCADE}` (defers, MSA-22). (ii) If any transfer nonetheless lands an actor's foot box inside a SOLID rectangle — a system-origin cut, a restore of an older save, a template defect — BDY-16 applies: the body is never displaced. PCI:650 already rules the door analogue (a system-origin close enters `CLOSING_BLOCKED` and retries); this GDD turns the mirror into a **named must-repeat for Modular Ship Assembly (now Designed and repeating it, MSA-21, MSA-22; recorded in 8.3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: was "provisional, undesigned")***: a SYSTEM-origin cut DEFERS while `actors_overlapping` is non-empty for the seam's two hatch rectangles, and the cut is preceded by the Pillar 2 tell window that Assembly and Adaptive Audio own (the 10 to 30 s escalating tell; the Graph's `W_MIN_WARNING_S` fairness gate), so a breach-driven cut can never separate a crewmate or seal one into a cap without a telegraphed window. How long a deferred cut may wait, and what Assembly does when the window expires with a crewmate still in the passage, are Assembly's (Open Question 10); Body supplies only the pure read. The no-displacement rule is unchanged and correct: the deferral prevents the overlap, it does not resolve one. **Struck:** a defensive deterministic push-out and its diagnostic, which contradict PCI:650 and P2. *Decides:* R7, LY-11, PCI:650, P2. (auto: hatch-cap fixture)

**BDY-21 — Mutator surface BM1-BM7, all Class A; every mutator returns OK or a FAULT_CODE; validation is a pure read.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the contract of this rule is rewritten; the earlier assumption that an apply cannot fail is struck, because it contradicted MSA-14, MSA-31 and AC-MSA-142)* Body publishes seven mutators — BM1 `place_actor`, BM2 `remove_actor`, BM3 `rebase_on_attach`, BM4 `rebase_on_detach`, BM5 `transfer_actor`, BM6 `set_body_velocity`, BM7 `set_body_pose` (added at the consistency pass 2026-10-27, routed from `web-map-and-transit.md` ASK-B1, WM-6) — each called only from Assembly's or Transit's single `apply`, AFTER the Layout mutator in the same `WriteScope` (KRN:197 names the three mutator owners; the order inside one scope, Graph then Layout then Body, is Assembly's contract (Modular Ship Assembly is Designed and repeats it: MSA-14, table T3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), implied by Layout returning the records Body consumes, LY-16, LY-17). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Every mutator returns a status; none is assumed to succeed.** GDScript has no throw and no catch, and `assert()` is compiled out of a release export, so a mutator that cannot honour its apply-time predicate has to say so in its return value (the caller's half is MSA-31, MSA-14 and AC-MSA-142). BM2 to BM7 return an `int`: `OK` (0) or a NEGATIVE `FAULT_CODE`, which is the negated Body reason constant of the `can_*` read that would have rejected the call (reason constants are positive ints, so `-BDY_PLACE_CAPACITY` is a `FAULT_CODE`). BM1 returns the allocated `actor_id` (an int >= 1) or a negative `FAULT_CODE`: one return channel, no out-parameter and no per-call allocation. `rc < 0` is a fault for every mutator. The caller's `apply` (Assembly's or Transit's) checks the status after EVERY Body call and, on the first negative value, calls the kernel's fault entry (MSA-31, ASK K2) and makes no further mutator call, so a failure inside `apply` moves the kernel to `FAULTED` (KRN:104). Body's mutators are not kernel-registered owner callables (they run inside the caller's `apply`); Body's kernel-registered callables (`body.integrate`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`) take the kernel's `ctx`, return their results through it and end `return ctx.complete()` (delegated ruling R3). What R8 calls "BM1 validates ..." is **published as pure `can_*` precondition reads** — `can_place`, `can_remove`, `can_rebase_attach`, `can_rebase_detach`, `can_transfer`, `can_set_velocity`, `can_set_pose` — that the caller's `validate` invokes before any mutator runs, exactly as the Graph's pure `can_join` serves weld validation; inside `apply` the same checks are re-evaluated as the apply-time predicate below, and every mutator is **check-then-write** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: it evaluates its WHOLE predicate before its first row write, so a call that returns a `FAULT_CODE` has written nothing (the tables, `next_actor_id`, the dirty set and the event queue are exactly as before the call, and no half-applied weld or cut exists). Every apply-time defect calls the injectable **`plan_mismatch_sink`**, a module-level `Callable` taking `(mutator_id, code)`: its default increments the counter `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, which is ACTIVE in every build, and in a debug build also calls `push_error`. No mutator path uses `assert()`, because a GDScript `assert` is compiled out of release and cannot be intercepted by a test; a test injects a recording sink and exercises every defect in the ordinary debug gdUnit4 runner (harness rule 1). The apply-time predicate per mutator is a mismatch with the pre-state its `can_*` read would have proven: BM1 any `can_place` reason; BM2 an unknown actor; BM3 the two ids equal or the surviving body not live in Layout; BM4 the old body not live, `new_body_id` not live in Layout, or a `moved_sections[]` member not owned by `new_body_id` (the call-order trap of BDY-23), or *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* a new pose row out of range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: this one is NOT a failing predicate; it is the saturate-and-continue branch of the split below)*; BM5 an unknown actor, an unknown destination or an arrival box inside a SOLID rectangle; BM6 an unknown body or a velocity out of range; BM7 an unknown body or a coordinate out of range. **The split per defect class *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.** (i) *Return-the-code class* (the call writes nothing and returns the `FAULT_CODE`; the caller faults the kernel): an unknown, equal or dead id (BM2 `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR`; BM3 and BM4 `BDY_REBASE_SAME_BODY` or `BDY_REBASE_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM5 `BDY_UNKNOWN_ACTOR` or `BDY_PLACE_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM6 `BDY_VEL_UNKNOWN_BODY`; BM7 `BDY_POSE_UNKNOWN_BODY`); a BM4 `moved_sections[]` member not owned by `new_body_id` (`BDY_REBASE_SECTION_NOT_OWNED`, the call-order trap of BDY-23); a BM3 or BM4 `frame_shift_px` off Layout's 24-px grid (`BDY_REBASE_SHIFT_OFF_GRID`); any rejected BM1, including an over-cap one (`BDY_PLACE_CAPACITY` and the other `can_place` reasons); a BM5 arrival box inside a SOLID rectangle (`BDY_PLACE_INSIDE_FOOTPRINT`); a BM6 velocity or BM7 coordinate out of range (`BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BDY_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE`; the call writes nothing, so no unloadable row can result). (ii) *Saturate-and-continue class* (the call completes and returns `OK`): **only BM4's new pose row**, where `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` or `vel_old` plus drift leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`; it saturates per BDY-23, the sink counts `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` (where applicable) and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`, and BM4 returns `OK`. The reason is the user's ruling that a death restarts from the last autosave: by the time BM4 runs the Graph and Layout have already applied the cut, and a row `restore` would reject (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`) would make the next autosave unloadable, so this branch is load-bearing and must not become a fault. Class (i) is checked first: a BM4 call that has both an unknown new body and a range overflow returns the code. *Consistency* after any call, including every call that returned a `FAULT_CODE`: `restore(snapshot())` accepts the block, actor ids are unique and below `next_actor_id`, and every `body_id` in either table is live in Layout; there is no exception (an over-cap BM1 is a returned code and writes no row, so no over-cap row can exist and Open Question 13 is closed). This *is* validate-then-apply (CR-9) with the two halves held by different owners. None of the `can_*` reads needs Layout's apply-time return record *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: except that `can_rebase_detach` takes the seam's `frame_shift_px` as a caller-supplied argument, below, exactly as `docked` does)*: each proves only that the bodies it names are live in Layout's pre-state, that ids differ and, for BM4, that the new pose row is in range (`can_rebase_detach(old_body_id, frame_shift_px)` proves that the old body is live in Layout *and, (Amended 2026-10-27 — design review), that the cut cannot produce a pose row `restore` would reject*: it answers `BDY_REBASE_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` on either axis and `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE` when `vel_old` plus the drift (BDY-28) leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK`; `frame_shift_px` is the value Layout's D.12 fixes for the seam (Assembly passes its own V3 `frame_shift_px`, the value its `detach_preview` produced, to this read, so the range guard runs on the real validate path; the Layout preview itself is optional, Open Question 34; Assembly's V4 row and AC-MSA-77 still show the one-argument form, which Assembly conforms to this signature because the registry's `body_mutators` is sourced here (G1); at apply time Layout's REAL record is authoritative as for every other mutator) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a fresh Layout `body_id` cannot already own a Body row, because `BDY_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BODY` rejects any Body id Layout does not hold, and an apply-time disagreement between a returned record and the pre-state returns its `FAULT_CODE` and is reported to the sink as `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH`); at `apply` time Assembly passes Layout's REAL record, which Body treats as authoritative. Body registers no player command type and subscribes to no Layout dirty keys. *Rejected:* Body reconciling from Layout's dirty keys inside its hook (a write outside a mutator; CR-9), and Layout calling Body (breaks the acyclic LY-18). Dirty keys use Layout's encoding `(KIND << 32) | id`, `BODY` 2 (the shared family) and a new `ACT` 4, with **explicit dirty marking in every mutator** (4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call the property setter — verified-from-docs, `breaking-changes.md` 4.6 to 4.7, "Packed array element writes"). The full interface is in States and Transitions. *Decides:* R8, CR-9, LY-18; P1 (no half-applied weld leaves an actor in a frame that does not exist). (auto) → ADR-BODY-02.

**BDY-23 — Detach transfer (BM4): the foot origin picks the side.** For each actor on the old body the side is the component whose section contains the foot ORIGIN on the detach tick (PCI:651, PCI:1001); a foot box straddling the seam is not split. Because BM4 runs after Layout's mutator, Layout has already re-based the moved sections, so Body evaluates containment against the **reconstructed pre-cut geometry**: for `s` in `moved_sections[]`, `offset_pre(s) = section_offset(s) + frame_shift_px`; for every other section of the old body `offset_pre(s) = section_offset(s)` (D.5; stated once as the call-order trap). Containment is by the section's FLOOR area (its rooms and the rectangles it owns, including its own 24-px hull footprint and hatch rectangles), never by bounding box, because hull-abutting sections have overlapping bounding boxes. Actors on `C_new`: `pos_curr -= frame_shift_px`, `body_id := new_body_id`, `pos_prev := pos_curr`, `sub := (0, 0)`, `last_octant` kept (harmless: `sub` is already zero, so a held key reads "no change"); emit `BODY_TRANSFER{detach}` with `frame_delta_px = -frame_shift_px` (3.7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Actors on `C_keep` are untouched. An origin lying in no section (an exterior gap, a defect) stays on `C_keep` and counts `BDY_TRANSFER_NO_SECTION`; this is a defect-only state, CI asserts it never occurs in a clean build (AC-BDY-29a), and its consequence is exterior exposure, never the last room's atmosphere (BDY-29, 8.3). BM4 creates the new body's pose row from the old body's (`world := world_old + frame_shift_px`, `vel := vel_old`, plus the default-zero detach drift of BDY-28), so a cut leaves both halves co-moving; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **the new row is always restorable.** The pose range is a restore rule (`BDY_RESTORE_POSE_RANGE`), so a BM4 that wrote an out-of-range row would make the next autosave unloadable and break BDY-21's `restore(snapshot())` guarantee and the death-restart path. The normal defence is `can_rebase_detach`'s `BDY_REBASE_POSE_OUT_OF_RANGE` and `BDY_VEL_OUT_OF_RANGE` (BDY-21) and Transit's re-origin discipline (WM-6 keeps every pose within `WEB_COORD_BUDGET_PX`, 1/32 of the limit). The apply-time net for a caller that ignored the read is the D.7 freeze rule applied to the new row: if `world_old + frame_shift_px` leaves the range the new `world` is saturated per axis to `±WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` and `vel` is set to `(0, 0)`; if `vel_old + drift` leaves `±VEL_MAX_PX_PER_TICK` it is saturated per axis; `BDY_WORLD_LIMIT` (where applicable) and `BDY_PLAN_MISMATCH` count through the sink and BM4 returns `OK`: this is the saturate-and-continue class of BDY-21, and every other BM4 defect returns its `FAULT_CODE` and writes nothing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. This is the one place a stored coordinate is saturated, it is defect-only, it touches the exterior pose alone (the interior bytes are unchanged, BDY-2), and the exterior `abs` conservation below is waived on that branch; the Controller clears `channel_ref` and keeps `octant`, `carry_ref` and `facing` (its rule, cited). The `sub` zeroing is a TRANSFER rule and does not conflict with BDY-31 (a restore is not a transfer). **Conservation law (the spike's falsifiable invariant):** with `abs(actor) = world(body_of(actor)) + pos_curr(actor)`, detach conserves `abs` exactly for every actor on either side; a weld conserves `abs` iff the docking invariant of BDY-27 holds; and **a weld followed by a cut of the same seam is not in general an identity on `pos_curr`** (detach re-bases to the section `m` with minimum id in `C_new`, LY D.12, while a weld shifts by the absorbed offset; the two coincide only when the absorbed body's section sat at its own frame origin), so any round-trip criterion asserts `abs` and the section-local position, never raw `pos_curr`. Fixture: Layout `fixture_chain` (chain 1 `(0, 0)`, 3 `(576, 96)`, 4 `(1056, 96)` cut at the (1, 3) seam: `frame_shift_px (576, 96)`, new offsets 3 `(0, 0)`, 4 `(480, 0)`). *Decides:* R7, LY-17, PCI:651; T3. (auto: D.5 fixture)

**MSA-21 — `CUT_BLOCKED`: a CHANNEL cut rejects, a CASCADE cut defers; it is a kept oracle.** *Rule:* this is Body's named must-repeat 1 (the hatch-cap hazard, BDY-24). If `actors_overlapping(body_id, [the seam's two hatch rectangles])` is non-empty, a `CHANNEL` cut **rejects** with `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED` at begin, at handoff and at completion (MSA-7), and a `CASCADE` cut defers (MSA-22). The ship never closes a seam on a crewmate. Body adds no push-out (BDY-24 struck it). The handoff and completion cue (the seam-cut family's one post-channel non-DONE cue, MSA-34): *the flame gutters and the seam holds*, and the channel has ended; the crewmate in the hatch is the witness; the `LOUD` was already pushed at DONE by Interaction (MSA-29). **Kept oracle:** `CUT_BLOCKED` reads true actor presence in the hatch, not module-body state, so it passes IA-11; it is deliberately a truth channel for hallucination classes (a) and (c) (a phantom entity is not an actor, a real person is), costs one attempt and zero time, and the Perception Filter must never wrap it. It is also a griefing vector in co-op (a crewmate can stand in the hatch to veto a cut), recorded as a Vertical Slice B concern `[VS-B]`. **The cutter's own body.** `actors_overlapping` lists every actor including the cutter, and each rectangle is `width_tiles * 48` by 24 px (96 x 24 px for the MVP pair), `REACH_PX` is 72 and the foot box is `FOOT_BOX_W` 16 by `FOOT_BOX_H` 8. If the `WELD_SOCKET` subject's anchor sat inside a rectangle, the cutter's own body would block their own cut at all three sites, a defect no unit test with a stub actor would find. Required resolution (a): Layout and Interaction place the subject's anchor and reach so that a legal lit stance exists outside both rectangles with at least one foot-box half-extent of clearance, enforced by an authoring lint `SOCKET_STANCE_BAND_EMPTY` (ASK L2; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:* **answered**: Layout carries the lint `SOCKET_STANCE_BAND_EMPTY` (LY-30) and the registered `SOCKET_STANCE_CLEARANCE_PX` 8 (Layout Tuning Knobs); the rectangle coordinates of AC-MSA-36 and 37 remain `[UNV]` until Layout publishes them). The alternative, an exclusion parameter on `actors_overlapping` (ASK to Body), is not preferred. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-36 (auto: reject at the three sites with a real second actor), AC-MSA-37 (spike: one actor at maximum legal reach starts a SEALED cut without `CUT_BLOCKED`; one foot-box into a rectangle fires it). *Pillar:* P4, P1, anti-pillars. *Decides:* advisor R10, R16; BDY-24; game-designer G5, G7.

On expiry with an actor still in the hatch rectangles the cut is **abandoned, never forced** ("the ship will not close a seam on a crewmate", BDY-24). `assembly.state` gains the deferral record `{seam_id, first_deferred_T}` at Vertical Slice; the field is reserved in schema v1. *Criterion:* AC-MSA-38 (auto, stub submitter: defer, apply when clear, abandon on expiry). *Pillar:* P2. *Alternative considered:* a scripted system cut for the breach rhythm in MVP — rejected (scope; the tell is not built). *Decides:* advisor R16.

If that predicate fires, the kernel faults and restarts from the pre-cut autosave, which functions as a refusal since the cut never persists and the player is never entombed — though this is a defect-only fallback path, not a clean refusal.

I'm concluding there's no separate crisis-cut path that bypasses validate: every cut, whether channel or cascade, routes through Assembly's seam_cut, and Layout's detach_section has exactly one caller. So Body's guard at apply time acts as the safety net, and the remaining question is scoping the minimal set of changes across Body and Layout's specs and acceptance criteria to reflect this.

Going with cap_rects, using the pre-cut frame from detach_preview since at BM4 apply time actors are still positioned in the old frame before being transferred. The check needs to happen before any writes occur, evaluating whether an actor's foot box intersects a rect it wasn't previously overlapping.

### D.11 Overlap exemption and `actors_overlapping`

The overlap exemption formula is defined as:

`ov(box, r) = max(0, min(box.x1, r.x1) - max(box.x0, r.x0)) * max(0, min(box.y1, r.y1) - max(box.y0, r.y0));     E = { r SOLID : ov(foot_box(pos_start), r) > 0 }  (fixed for the tick);     a 1-px sub-step to box_after is admitted  iff  for every r in E:  ov(box_after, r) <= ov(box_before, r)`

Every rectangle not in `E` stays fully solid, so an exempt actor cannot walk into a wall it was not already inside. The test is **per rectangle, not total** (CP-1): on the `fixture_airlock` hull-line geometry a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles keeps its TOTAL overlap while stepping across their shared edge, which a total-area test would admit and the per-rectangle test refuses. Nothing shoves: `pos` is unchanged on every tick the actor does not step.

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `box`, `box_before`, `box_after` | half-open rect | D.2 | `foot_box` at the sub-step | the foot box before and after one 1-px sub-step on either axis |
| `r` | half-open rect | body frame | Layout's `solid_in` result (SOLID filter) | a candidate rectangle |
| `ov(box, r)` | int | 0 to `FOOT_BOX_W * FOOT_BOX_H` = 128 | calculated | overlapped cells |
| `E` | set of rectangles | 0 to `K` (D.12) | calculated at the start of the actor's tick | rectangles the start box already intersects; empty on every ordinary tick |

**Output Range:** `E` empty means ordinary sweeping. For a PARTIAL overlap any sub-step with a component away from a rectangle shrinks that rectangle's `ov`, so the box leaves in a bounded number of ticks and can never deepen. A sub-step is also refused when its destination foot origin lies in no section of the actor's body (D.10), so no exempt step leaves the hull. Residuals (defect-only, BDY-16): a box wholly inside one rectangle has constant `ov` until an edge crosses out (it may exit either side provided the destination origin is in a section of the body); a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles can only slide along the shared edge or back out; a hatch-cap actor whose only shrinking direction leaves the body cannot leave (the cap trap). Each actor-tick on which `E` is evaluated non-empty (plus each detection event that finds `E` non-empty) increments `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` (BDY-

**Example (BDY-16 hatch cap, after a SYSTEM-origin cut):** `pos = (690, 282)`, box `[682, 698) x [282, 290)`, plate `[672, 696) x [240, 336)`: `ov = (696 - 682) * 8 = 112`. West (box `[681, 697)`): `ov = 15 * 8 = 120 > 112`, refused. East (box `[683, 699)`): `13 * 8 = 104`, admitted. North or south: `14 * 8 = 112`, admitted. Walking east at `V_WALK` 2 the actor reaches `pos.x = 695` (692, 694, 695 over three ticks) and stops: the sub-step to 696 passes the overlap test (`ov` 64) but its destination origin `(696, 282)` lies in plate B's footprint, which left with its section and is in no section of this body, so exit containment refuses it. `actors_overlapping(body_id, rects[]) = { a on body_id :  there exists r in rects with ov(foot_box(pos_curr(a)), r) > 0 },  in ascending actor_id`

**BDY-16 — Overlap exemption: the body is never displaced, and an exempt actor can only leave.** Let `E` be the set of SOLID rectangles the actor's foot box intersects **at the start of the actor's tick** (fixed for that tick). Members of `E` arise from a door leaf that closed under the actor, a system-origin cut that capped a hatch under it, a restore of an older save against a changed template, or a template defect. For an actor with a non-empty `E`, a 1-px sub-step on either axis is admitted iff **for every `r` in `E`, `|box_after ∩ r| <= |box_before ∩ r|`** (overlap measured in cells; D.11 states `ov(r)`) **and the destination foot origin lies in a section of the actor's body (exit containment, below)**; every rectangle not in `E` stays fully solid, so an exempt actor cannot walk into a wall it was not already inside. The test is per rectangle, not total: on the `fixture_airlock` hull-line geometry a box astride two abutting exempt rectangles `[672, 696)` and `[696, 720)` keeps its TOTAL overlap at 128 cells while stepping east (one rectangle loses a column, the other gains one), so a total-area test would let it cross the hull line, while the per-rectangle test refuses that step because the east rectangle's own overlap grows; every move along the shared edge (both overlaps unchanged) and every move away (both shrink) stays admitted. `E` is computed afresh each tick from the current box (no stored flag; nothing persisted or hashed). Each exempt actor-tick increments `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` (read 0 in a clean build) and, in debug, fires `diag.actor_in_footprint` (PIPE:727). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What "exempt actor-tick" counts (option (a), adopted).** `E` is computed from a `solid_in` query, and a stationary actor issues none (BDY-9), so the counter increments **once per actor-tick in which `E` was evaluated and found non-empty** (a tick on which the actor requested a non-zero step, so the query ran), **plus once at each detection event whose start-of-tick box test finds `E` non-empty** (placement, a transfer, a weld or cut for every actor on the touched bodies, `post_restore`): a detection event on an actor whose box intersects nothing adds nothing, so a clean weld, cut or restore leaves the counter at 0 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier wording read as an unconditional increment per event)*. input.notes: Plan only; nothing edited. The three blockers resolve as follows. (1) Seat binding: the kernel owns the binding table, so under G6 the kernel adds the missing step. It rebuilds the PlayerId-to-entities half as the last atomic action of every LOADING (restore, death stub and new game), from owner-registered pure 'binding sources' (Body seat_bindings(), Emitter beam_bindings()), so the death-restart loop closes with no Save/Load step; Save/Load and the Suit/Emitter 'session owner re-enters' wording only conform, and Body promotes AC-BDY-6/138 to its epic's integration closure gate (no longer BLOCKED-ON). The peer-to-PlayerId half stays session state and is untouched, so kernel seq counters are not reset. (2) Canonical bytes: kernel D.12 TLV is the only definition (G1). Body keeps only the snapshot payload SHAPE (a 5-key Dictionary of ints and two int Arrays), drops encode_s32/s64, and H_actors becomes canonical_encode(payload['actors']), a per-key comparison (the kernel hashes per block, never per table), using a new pure kernel helper canonical_encode. The golden file is recomputed from the TLV rules for 2 bodies and 3 actors: 9 + 86 + 279 + 117 + 27 = 518 bytes, replacing 208; the actors key alone is 279 bytes. (3) ENTOMB: no cut path bypasses Assembly's V5 (CHANNEL rejects, CASCADE defers or is abandoned, and detach_section has one caller), so Layout's 'crisis cut' is the CASCADE cut. Body rules refuse rather than eject (P2) and adds a BM4 apply-time net: a fifth argument rects[], supplied by a new rects[] field on Layout's detach_section record, and a new reason BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP. can_rebase_detach and Assembly's V4 and reason order stay unchanged. Because a cut can no longer create the cap trap, Body's trap fixtures (AC-BDY-29, 29b, 29c, 43) are re-based on a restore. toolu_01YLDZ85pKVAKvj8DFVAjweh.notes: Plan only; nothing edited. The three blockers resolve as follows. (1) Seat binding: the kernel owns the binding table, so under G6 the kernel adds the missing step. It rebuilds the PlayerId-to-entities half as the last atomic action of every LOADING (restore, death stub and new game), from owner-registered pure 'binding sources' (Body seat_bindings(), Emitter beam_bindings()), so the death-restart loop closes with no Save/Load step; Save/Load and the Suit/Emitter 'session owner re-enters' wording only conform, and Body promotes AC-BDY-6/138 to its epic's integration closure gate (no longer BLOCKED-ON). The peer-to-PlayerId half stays session state and is untouched, so kernel seq counters are not reset. (2) Canonical bytes: kernel D.12 TLV is the only definition (G1). Body keeps only the snapshot payload SHAPE (a 5-key Dictionary of ints and two int Arrays), drops encode_s32/s64, and H_actors becomes canonical_encode(payload['actors']), a per-key comparison (the kernel hashes per block, never per table), using a new pure kernel helper canonical_encode. The golden file is recomputed from the TLV rules for 2 bodies and 3 actors: 9 + 86 + 279 + 117 + 27 = 518 bytes, replacing 208; the actors key alone is 279 bytes. (3) ENTOMB: no cut path bypasses Assembly's V5 (CHANNEL rejects, CASCADE defers or is abandoned, and detach_section has one caller), so Layout's 'crisis cut' is the CASCADE cut. Body rules refuse rather than eject (P2) and adds a BM4 apply-time net: a fifth argument rects[], supplied by a new rects[] field on Layout's detach_section record, and a new reason BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP. can_rebase_detach and Assembly's V4 and reason order stay unchanged. Because a cut can no longer create the cap trap, Body's trap fixtures (AC-BDY-29, 29b, 29c, 43) are re-based on a restore. Registry requests for the orchestrator or registry writer, since the registry is not a GDD target: (a) body_state.canonical_bytes rewritten to the TLV payload shape, with the 'written by hand-written encode_s32/encode_s64' text struck; (b) body_mutators: BM4 gains the fifth argument cap_rects[], the reasons list gains BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP, and the pure_reads list is unchanged; (c) state_hash and canonical_bytes entry: add the canonical_encode helper, and a kernel binding_source registration entry with Body and Emitter as consumers. No epoch (R13/R14) text appears in Body (0 grep hits for restore_epoch, EPOCH_DURABLE or fresh-process), so this blocker needs no epoch edits. The binding rebuild runs inside LOADING after the R14 pre-restore staging step has completed, so it does not interact with it. The R13/R14 targets belong to the other blockers' plans.

data.notes: Plan only; nothing edited. The three blockers resolve as follows. (1) Seat binding: the kernel owns the binding table, so under G6 the kernel adds the missing step. It rebuilds the PlayerId-to-entities half as the last atomic action of every LOADING (restore, death stub and new game), from owner-registered pure 'binding sources' (Body seat_bindings(), Emitter beam_bindings()), so the death-restart loop closes with no Save/Load step; Save/Load and the Suit/Emitter 'session owner re-enters' wording only conform, and Body promotes AC-BDY-6/138 to its epic's integration closure gate (no longer BLOCKED-ON). The peer-to-PlayerId half stays session state and is untouched, so kernel seq counters are not reset. (2) Canonical bytes: kernel D.12 TLV is the only definition (G1). Body keeps only the snapshot payload SHAPE (a 5-key Dictionary of ints and two int Arrays), drops encode_s32/s64, and H_actors becomes canonical_encode(payload['actors']), a per-key comparison (the kernel hashes per block, never per table), using a new pure kernel helper canonical_encode. The golden file is recomputed from the TLV rules for 2 bodies and 3 actors: 9 + 86 + 279 + 117 + 27 = 518 bytes, replacing 208; the actors key alone is 279 bytes. (3) ENTOMB: no cut path bypasses Assembly's V5 (CHANNEL rejects, CASCADE defers or is abandoned, and detach_section has one caller), so Layout's 'crisis cut' is the CASCADE cut. Body rules refuse rather than eject (P2) and adds a BM4 apply-time net: a fifth argument rects[], supplied by a new rects[] field on Layout's detach_section record, and a new reason BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP. can_rebase_detach and Assembly's V4 and reason order stay unchanged. Because a cut can no longer create the cap trap, Body's trap fixtures (AC-BDY-29, 29b, 29c, 43) are re-based on a restore. Registry requests for the orchestrator or registry writer, since the registry is not a GDD target: (a) body_state.canonical_bytes rewritten to the TLV payload shape, with the 'written by hand-written encode_s32/encode_s64' text struck; (b) body_mutators: BM4 gains the fifth argument cap_rects[], the reasons list gains BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP, and the pure_reads list is unchanged; (c) state_hash and canonical_bytes entry: add the canonical_encode helper, and a kernel binding_source registration entry with Body and Emitter as consumers. No epoch (R13/R14) text appears in Body (0 grep hits for restore_epoch, EPOCH_DURABLE or fresh-process), so this blocker needs no epoch edits. The binding rebuild runs inside LOADING after the R14 pre-restore staging step has completed, so it does not interact with it. The R13/R14 targets belong to the other blockers' plans.
